title: Philadelphia Fed Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations (ATSIX), November 2026 — 2:00 p.m. ET on November opex Friday, a model-fitted expected-CPI curve whose 118 published horizons are three free numbers
source: EST: philadelphiafed.org/calendar-of-events, re-fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 131,096 bytes) and parsed as data this session — the embedded release payload holds 237 rows across 18 release families, of which exactly 12 are ATSIX, every one at 2:00 p.m., verbatim 'Aruoba Term Structure of Inflation Expectations | Nov 20 2026 | 2:00 p.m.'. Weekday arithmetic reproduced this session, NOT recalled: ten of the twelve rows (Jan 30, Feb 27, Mar 27, Apr 24, May 29, Jun 26, Jul 31, Aug 28, Sep 25, Oct 30) are their month's LAST Friday. December 29 is a Tuesday because December's last Friday is 2026-12-25, Christmas Day, a federal holiday on which the Reserve Banks are shut — airtight. NOVEMBER 20 IS THE THIRD FRIDAY, seven days ahead of the last Friday (2026-11-27), and the proposal's Thanksgiving explanation does NOT survive this session's check: 2026-11-27 is not a federal holiday (only Thanksgiving Day, 2026-11-26, is) and Reserve Bank offices are open that day, so a half-day equity session does not explain moving a 2:00 p.m. research release a full week early. The date is read from the publisher's own calendar row and is consistent with the ATSIX technical note's stated timing constraint (publication follows the 15-calendar-day average nominal yield curve of the vintage month, philadelphiafed.org/-/media/frbp/assets/surveys-and-data/atsix/atsix-technical-document.pdf, fetched direct 2026-09-09 HTTP 200, 61,282 bytes, text extracted this session), but NO rule derives it. Corroborated on an ATSIX-SPECIFIC surface only for the one date both pages carry: the ATSIX landing page (philadelphiafed.org/surveys-and-data/real-time-data-research/atsix, fetched direct 2026-09-09 HTTP 200, 36,815 bytes) stamps itself '28 Aug '26', matching the calendar's Aug 28 row and the published workbook's last vintage (2026-08) exactly; that page carries no forward dates and defers to the shared calendar. Filed estimate on four counts: market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for a regional Reserve Bank's own data schedule (FED: covers the federalreserve.gov FOMC calendar only), this lane never self-confirms an event it discovered in-sweep, no ATSIX-specific page carries the November date, and the November row is the single 2026 row no rule explains
notes: CANONICAL entry written 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read the one proposal that existed for this id (proposals/aruoba-inflation-term-structure-2026-11-20.from-philly-fed-price-inflation-expectations-q4-2026-11-25.json, filed 2026-09-09) and discharged all three tasks it assigned. (a) PARTIAL — see `source`: the date is re-read and the weekday arithmetic reproduced, an ATSIX-specific surface corroborates the calendar on the one date both carry, and the proposal's holiday explanation for the November row is REFUTED; no rule derives 2026-11-20, which is why the entry stays estimate. (b) SETTLED — ATSIX is MODEL OUTPUT, not a survey. The publisher's own words: 'created by using a factor model to optimally combine major surveys — the Survey of Professional Forecasters... and the Blue Chip Economic Indicators and Blue Chip Financial Forecasts'. It forecasts CPI as a continuously compounded annualized rate, horizons 3 to 120 months. (c) DECLINE THE FAMILY, ON MEASUREMENT. The published curve's 118 horizon columns are a function of three free numbers: regressing each column on [1, level, slope, curvature] across all 344 vintages gives R-squared >= 0.99924 at EVERY horizon (worst h=120; mean 0.99964), and the technical note's own equation with tau1=0 reproduces all 40,592 published points at RMSE 0.0024pp, max error 0.042pp. 'Which part of the curve moved' therefore has exactly three answers, not 118 — the proposal filed this event for a resolution the instrument does not have. And the long end updates four months a year, not twelve: mean absolute month-over-month change in the 10-year point is 0.0599pp in Mar/Jun/Oct/Dec versus 0.0319pp in the other eight months (ratio 1.88, Welch t=5.86, n=343), and 0.0698 versus 0.0293 on the level factor itself (ratio 2.38, t=7.60), surviving the post-2016 model-change subsample. NOVEMBER IS NOT ONE OF THE FOUR: across 28 Novembers the 10-year point's median absolute move is 0.0293pp — about three basis points — and only 2022 ever exceeded 0.10pp. This row is kept because it is the researched one and its ledger retires the family on the record; the other eleven 2027 ATSIX rows are declined and should not be proposed. Impact LOW and symbols [] on grounds this ledger measures rather than inherits: no house playbook is macro-keyed, no tracked name carries an expectations-curve channel, the 14:00 ET slot is November opex Friday (opex-2026-11-20, medium, confirmed) with 40 tracked events inside five days, and the instrument's own stated use — pricing securities linked to inflation expectations at arbitrary horizons — is served continuously and for free by the breakeven curve, which the 10-year TIPS auction (treasury-10y-tips-2026-11-19) prices with real money the day before. This is an ESTIMATE — it widens caution, licenses nothing, and the ledger's stance is a permanent stand-aside.
